premiums are a waste, I'd rather keep the money in savings

According to MoSPI/NSO, NSS 80th round press note, a median private‑hospital stay costs ₹24,000 (≈$248) out of pocket. The average health claim paid in 2024–25 was about ₹28,900 (≈$299) (as reported by IndiaMedToday). Those amounts can quickly eat into savings. Does that change how you see the value of a premium?
Well hospital costs double every five years anyway, right?
I don't have a source for that, so I won't state it.
So you agree I should get insurance then?

Employer medical plan costs are projected to rise 11.5% in 2026 after a 13% increase in 2025 (Aon, 2026 Global Medical Trend Rates, India release). In 2022–23 households paid about 43% of total health spending directly out of pocket (National Health Accounts Estimates 2022–23, NHSRC/MoHFW). Does that affect how you view the trade‑off between premiums and potential out‑of‑pocket bills?
